changes: Remove four rules delegating to the ESLint engine; the only enabled one is replaced by stock eslint/logical-assignment-operators.
Remove their engine-importing utility barrel export.
Point standalone token/scope utility imports to the copied licensed utility source.
Expose exactly the retained syntax rules through a native definePlugin entry point.
Read VariableDeclaration.kind when the native scope definition omits kind.
Keep only package identity, documentation and ESM metadata used by the source port; remove unused original scripts, exports and dependency declarations.

Expose exact pinned prefer-top-level-await instead of the stock rule because the maintained upstream implementation retains the Zod schema catch fallback fix (upstream PR3005). Preserve its syntactic z/schema/*Schema detection and async-call suggestion; unknown custom catch methods are not type-resolved.

Extend the maintained Boolean helper with genuine same-file lexical binding evidence for explicitly annotated, nonoptional Boolean properties in local TypeScript object literals. Imported, inferred, optional and named property contracts remain unresolved; no checker or scope facade is introduced.

Expose the exact pinned prefer-number-properties and prefer-logical-operator-over-ternary implementations instead of their stock counterparts. Preserve no-radix/static decimal parseInt exemptions, checkNaN/checkInfinity options, Boolean ternary diagnostics and maintained fix restrictions in TypeScript; genuine native lexical bindings preserve shadowing and explicitly annotated Boolean tests. No rule-body rewrite or checker facade is introduced.

Expose exact pinned no-useless-spread and no-invalid-fetch-options instead of their stock counterparts. Preserve typed-array-to-Array conversions and unknown dynamic fetch methods while retaining actual redundant Array spreads and invalid GET/HEAD bodies; no source-body, severity, option or scope changes.

Replace prefer-combined-guards parser-service-dependent exclusion of nonliteral exits with a direct conservative AST exclusion, including process.exit arguments. The original TypeScript parser also excluded these in syntax-only JavaScript. Literal and empty exits, labels, comments and checkCompoundConditions options remain supported. Nonliteral JavaScript optimizations previously available under Espree are excluded because native syntax alone cannot establish flow/type safety; remove the redundant tagged-template walk.

Expose exact pinned require-module-specifiers instead of the stock rule. Preserve valid sole module markers, remove only redundant markers, and retain empty-import diagnostics and side-effect imports; no rule-body rewrite or dummy export is introduced.

Retain Unicorn 76's intentional exclusion of ternaries with two Boolean-literal branches. Older Unicorn 74 reported same-reference literal cases such as true ? true : false; genuine Unicorn 76 and the native source port both exclude them. This is an upstream version change, not an AST or plugin compatibility failure.

inactiveLegacyRules.no-shorthand-property-overrides: Only CSS Block visitors; original policy installs no CSS language.
inactiveLegacyRules.no-missing-local-resource: Only CSS, HTML, Markdown visitors; original policy installs no languages for those formats.
